title: Even-moment coefficient sum decomposition
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $P$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. For nonnegative integers $r,l$, define $G_l=\binom{2r}{2l}\bigl(1/\sqrt{2r-1}\bigr)^{2l}\mathbb E_P[X^{2l}]-\binom{r}{l}$. If $j\le r$ and $G_l=0$ for every nonnegative integer $l<j$, then for every $t\in\mathbb R$, $\sum_{l=0}^{r}G_l t^{2l}=G_jt^{2j}+\sum_{j<l\le r}G_l t^{2l}$.
hypotheses_covered: The coefficient gap $G_l$ vanishes for every nonnegative integer $l<j$
